title: ConTSG-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for Conditional Time Series Generation
claim: Conditional generation spans diverse conditioning modalities and abstraction levels, all feeding one generator that produces time series.
layout: 3 stacked bands, top-to-bottom; center row flows left-to-right through generator
description: The figure has three horizontal bands. The top green band, labeled Modality, shows three condition types: a dashed text box reading 'Variate 0 is a generally increasing trend with...' with a TXT file icon, an Attribute/Value table (trend: up), and a one-hot class-label vector with a tag icon. The middle row flows left to right: a yellow-outlined 'Condition c ∈ C' box with arrows up and down, then a rounded 'Conditional Generator p_θ(x|c)' box, then a 'Time Series' plot showing a rising blue temperature curve and the notation x̂ ∈ R^{L×F} ~ p_θ(x|c). The bottom blue band, labeled Semantic Abstraction, contrasts Morphological text ('increasing trend with moderate volatility...') with Conceptual text ('The current weather is clear...'). It uses a sketching-hand icon and a person with a lightbulb icon. The eye goes first to the central condition-to-generator-to-series flow.
caption: Conditional time series generation with varying conditioning modalities (text, attribute, class label) and semantic abstraction levels (morphological vs. conceptual).
abstract: Conditional time series generation plays a critical role in addressing data scarcity and enabling causal analysis in real-world applications. Despite its increasing importance, the field lacks a standardized and systematic benchmarking framework for evaluating generative models across diverse conditions. To address this gap, we introduce the Conditional Time Series Generation Benchmark (ConTSG-Bench). ConTSG-Bench comprises a large-scale, well-aligned dataset spanning diverse conditioning modalities and levels of semantic abstraction, first enabling systematic evaluation of representative generation methods across these dimensions with a comprehensive suite of metrics for generation fidelity and condition adherence. Both the quantitative benchmarking and in-depth analyses of conditional generation behaviors have revealed the traits and limitations of the current approaches, highlighting critical challenges and promising research directions, particularly with respect to precise structural controllability and downstream task utility under complex conditions.
